s50l:S1Q04F.q: How would you reduce the sorting cost for millions of customers while preserving the tie rule?
s50l:S1Q04F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-A
s50l:S1Q04F.spoken: I’d switch from a full sort to a min-heap approach, which drops the complexity from O(N log N) to O(N log K). For the tie-breaking, I’d store tuples of (score, tie-breaker-value) in the heap; the comparison logic naturally handles the tie-breaker when the primary score matches. If the dataset is too large for memory, I’d partition the data and use a distributed approach or database-level indexing to handle the heavy lifting before the final merge.

s50l:S1Q06F.q: How would you index those tables, and what changes if historical records can be corrected after ingestion?
s50l:S1Q06F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-A
s50l:S1Q06F.spoken: I’d start with a composite index on customer_id and timestamp to optimize those time-series range lookups. If historical records can be corrected, I’d implement a Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 pattern. Instead of overwriting, I’d add valid_from and valid_to timestamps, which lets us maintain full auditability and reconstruct the exact state of the data for any past inference.

s50l:S2Q05F.q: An example where that greedy policy gives poor coverage, and tell me how you would incorporate redundancy or multi hop dependencies.
s50l:S2Q05F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-A
s50l:S2Q05F.spoken: Greedy selection often leads to redundancy bias, where the top-k chunks are semantically identical. For instance, if I ask to compare Product A and Product B's revenue, but the top results all focus on Product A, the model lacks the context for Product B. To fix this, I use Maximal Marginal Relevance—or MMR—to penalize similarity to previously selected chunks, forcing diversity. For multi-hop dependencies, I avoid flat retrieval entirely; I use agentic query decomposition to break the prompt into sub-questions, or a graph-based retrieval that traverses relationships between entities to ensure we actually capture the full path needed for the answer.

s50l:S2Q08F.q: How do you prove the replacement index is sufficiently complete and current before you send production traffic to it?
s50l:S2Q08F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-A
s50l:S2Q08F.spoken: I validate the new index by running it in shadow mode alongside the production one, capturing real-world queries to compare retrieval performance. I use an LLM-as-judge pipeline to evaluate the recall and relevance of the retrieved chunks against a gold set, while simultaneously running deterministic checks to ensure the document count and metadata coverage match the source database. I only cut over once the new index demonstrates parity or improvement in both retrieval accuracy and latency metrics.
